image_description: A close-up, slightly blurry underwater shot of a lionfish. The image focuses on the head and the expansive, fan-like pectoral fins. The fish displays characteristic red and white vertical striping. The dorsal spines are visible but somewhat blended with the background due to motion blur or focus issues. The eye is prominent on the left side.

checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The head is clearly visible on the left, showing a large eye and the general shape of a wide mouth, consistent with lionfish anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Laterally compressed body with moderately sized proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The angle is a close-up profile; the full lateral compression and body proportions are difficult to verify definitively as the rear of the fish is out of frame or obscured by fins.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Brightly striped coloration in red, white, brown, or black bands.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Distinct red/maroon and white vertical stripes are clearly visible on the head and fin membranes.
Image resolution and softness prevent verification of individual small scales.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Dorsal fin with numerous elongated venomous spines that fan outward like mane.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Elongated spines are visible along the top edge, though they blend into the blue background due to blur.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Large fan-like pectoral fins with elongated rays.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dominant feature of the image is the large, translucent pectoral fin with distinct elongated rays fanning out.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pelvic fins also with elongated spines.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pelvic fins are located on the ventral side and are not clearly distinguishable in this specific crop/angle.

artifact_observations.location: Entire image, especially fin edges and background
artifact_observations.reasoning: Significant motion blur or out-of-focus softness affects the entire image, reducing structural clarity. While this may be photographic style, in AI generation it often masks structural inconsistencies.
Some fin rays appear to merge or fade into the background without clear termination points, suggesting slight 'melting' or lack of physical definition typical of generative artifacts.
The tips of the dorsal spines are indistinct and seem to dissolve into the blue water rather than having sharp, defined ends.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the species classification given the visual ambiguity caused by blur.
To check if the complex, thin fin rays are topologically connected to the body or if they float/fade unnaturally.
To assess if the blur is natural photographic motion blur or AI-generated smearing artifacts.

focus_areas: Connectivity of fin rays to the body
Sharpness and definition of dorsal spines
Consistency of stripe patterns across curved surfaces
